notes: Historical BEN tickets with merged, known-good solutions. Each base commit is the first parent of the commit that solved it, so the tree a cell starts from is the tree the historical author started from. A canary repository is a mirror of source_repo whose default branch is pinned at the case's base_commit; every check runs by `bash -c` in the root of the published head and must exit 0.

cases.title: Redistribute regression_test.go into the topic files that already exist

known_good.summary: Deleted internal/orchestrator/regression_test.go and redistributed its 53 tests across topic files, four of them new, moving bodies unchanged. Measured: the sorted set of Test names in internal/orchestrator is 337 names at the base and the same 337 afterwards.

checks.why: acceptance bullet 1: the pile is deleted, not shrunk and not left as a stub

checks.run: names() { for f in $(git ls-tree -r --name-only "$1" internal/orchestrator); do git show "$1:$f" | grep -o "^func Test[A-Za-z0-9_]*"; done | sort; }; diff <(names bd77c4ab8487df3c7a60bc7e9f5105276532a4b5) <(grep -ho "^func Test[A-Za-z0-9_]*" internal/orchestrator/*_test.go | sort)
checks.why: acceptance bullet 2: the sorted set of Test names is byte-identical to the base's, so the redistribution dropped none. A count would pass with one test lost and another added, which is why this diffs the names
the ticket's last bullet, and this repository's definition of green

cases.title: Tracker adapter: only Get and the content read classify a 404 as ErrIssueNotFound

known_good.summary: Decided reads classify absence and writes do not, documented the sentinel on exactly those methods, and mapped 404 there in the GitHub adapter. Measured against the base: mentions of ErrIssueNotFound go 3 to 6 in internal/core/core.go and 1 to 5 in the adapter — while internal/fake's go 5 to 4, because the fake had been classifying where the adapter does not. That is why no check here counts the fake: the known-good direction there is down.

checks.run: base=$(git show f3d885858147e10e47cce2c100fb7ee14b9b6bc6:internal/core/core.go | grep -c ErrIssueNotFound); [ "$(grep -c ErrIssueNotFound internal/core/core.go)" -gt "$base" ]
checks.why: acceptance bullet 2: core.TrackerAdapter names the sentinel on more methods than the two that carried it at the base. Compared against the base rather than against a number, because the base is not zero

checks.run: base=$(git show f3d885858147e10e47cce2c100fb7ee14b9b6bc6:internal/tracker/github/adapter.go | grep -c ErrIssueNotFound); [ "$(grep -c ErrIssueNotFound internal/tracker/github/adapter.go)" -gt "$base" ]
checks.why: acceptance bullet 3: the adapter maps 404 to the sentinel somewhere it did not at the base
the ticket's last bullet, and where bullet 4 has to land: 'a test asserts the classification and its absence' is a test in the tree, so make check is what runs it

cases.title: Bound and report the per-tick API request budget

known_good.summary: A per-tick budget the transport meters and the adapter enforces at two points, 40 billed requests per tick, opened per tick through core.RequestBudget; and a cache that evicts least-recently-used under an entry and byte bound instead of flushing. Measured against the base: `clear(c.entries)` and `maxCacheEntries = 512` are gone from internal/tracker/github, and adapter.go's mentions of a budget go 2 to 31.

checks.why: acceptance bullet 2: overflow no longer flushes the whole cache. The directory test is not decoration — a grep for something absent from a directory that is also absent would pass while measuring nothing

checks.run: base=$(git show 92cc85c6a30255cd0c1eaa6fa5f9aa913f12d00b:internal/tracker/github/adapter.go | grep -ic budget); [ "$(grep -ic budget internal/tracker/github/adapter.go)" -gt "$base" ]
checks.why: acceptance bullet 1: the adapter says more about a request budget than it did at the base — a necessary condition of enforcing and reporting one, and the base already says it twice
the ticket's last bullet, and this repository's definition of green
